titles.title: The Letter
titles.plot: In 2002, Larry Raymond, mayor of Lewiston, Maine, sends letters to more than 1,000 refugees from Somalia asking them to tell other Somalis not to move to the city. The resulting firestorm reveals an America divided on issues of immigration and race, as Raymond's letter receives condemnation from community leaders but support from white supremacist groups. Several months after the original letter, those for and against ethnic diversity converge on Lewiston for a protest and counter-protest.

titles.title: Rank
titles.plot: Filmmaker John Hyams follows three rodeo cowboys as they vie for the Professional Bull Riding Championship in Las Vegas. Justin McBride is a third-generation bull rider; Mike Lee, 21, is a born-again Christian; and Adriano Moraes has been in the sport since he was 18. The three struggle through the danger, pain and injury in their quest for the prize.

titles.title: Spellbound
titles.plot: Eight youthful competitors, sponsored by their hometown newspapers, travel with their families to Washington, D.C., to compete in the 1999 Scripps National Spelling Bee. Now in the national spotlight and under heavy pressure to perform from parents, teachers and their audience, the children struggle to advance toward the championship -- and its accompanying scholarships and cash prizes -- while approaching competitive spelling with the focus and intensity of Olympic athletes.

titles.title: Suicide Killers
titles.plot: Filmmaker Pierre Rehov explores the phenomenon of Arab terrorists who deploy themselves as bombs. Through interviews with family members and those whose efforts to detonate their bombs were thwarted, Rehov attempts to understand the motivations of this particular breed of terrorist.

titles.title: 56 Up
titles.plot: Continuing a project he began in 1964, filmmaker Michael Apted revisits his original subjects and sees how their lives are progressing now that they are 56 years old.

titles.title: A Space Program
titles.plot: Artist Tom Sachs and his team build an entire space program from scratch for a handmade journey to Mars.

titles.title: A Suitable Girl
titles.plot: Young women in India struggle to maintain their identities amid pressure to marry.

titles.title: Ali & Cavett: The Tale of the Tapes
titles.original_title: Ali & Cavett: The Tale of the Tapes
titles.plot: The life and times of Muhammad Ali are shown through the lens of his numerous appearances on "The Dick Cavett Show."

images.caption: Ali & Cavett: The Tale of the Tapes (2018)

titles.title: All the Rage
titles.plot: Dr. John Sarno battles America's pain epidemic.

titles.title: American Circumcision
titles.plot: Activists protest the widespread practice of nonreligious circumcision.

titles.title: Bedlam
titles.plot: A journey into the world of mental illness.

titles.title: Chasing Madoff
titles.plot: Securities analyst Harry Markopolos and his team of investigators spent 10 years trying to blow the lid off Bernie Madoff's devastating Ponzi scheme.

titles.title: El Bulli: Cooking in Progress
titles.plot: Chef Ferran Adrià spends half the year making new culinary creations for his restaurant.

titles.title: End of the Century
titles.plot: Joey, Johnny and Dee Dee -- better known as The Ramones -- changed the course of rock history with their rebellious punk ethos and minimalist approach to songwriting, and in the process became counterculture icons. "End of the Century" follows the Queens kids from their earliest underground gigs in the 1970s to their induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2002, featuring rare archive concert footage and candid interviews with the band members.

titles.title: Erase and Forget
titles.plot: The life of James Gordon Gritz, one of the most decorated Vietnam veterans.

titles.title: Fade to Black
titles.plot: This documentary focuses on the massively popular rap artist Jay-Z. The film's centerpiece is the hip-hop icon's sold-out 2003 performance at Madison Square Garden. Intended as a farewell concert, the show presents hits such as "Hard Knock Life" and "Crazy in Love," and features numerous guest artists, most notably Jay-Z's girlfriend, Beyoncé. The film also includes interviews with the rapper himself, behind-the-scenes footage and clips of Jay-Z during the recording process.

titles.title: Gottfried Helnwein & the Dreaming Child
titles.plot: Conflict erupts backstage between the Israeli Opera and artist Gottfried Helnwein regarding a casting choice for a production of the opera "The Child Dreams."

titles.title: A Great Day in Harlem
titles.plot: On a summer morning in 1958, photographer Art Kane assembled a remarkable array of leading jazz musicians in New York City's Harlem neighborhood for a group picture. This acclaimed documentary explores the story behind the photograph's creation, featuring interviews with some of the featured performers, who include Dizzy Gillespie, Sonny Rollins, Art Blakey, Hank Jones and Milt Hinton. The film is enhanced by footage taken by Hinton himself, who was also an accomplished photographer.

titles.title: Greenwich Village: Music That Defined a Generation
titles.original_title: Greenwich Village: Music That Defined a Generation
titles.plot: Interviews with Pete Seeger, Kris Kristofferson, Judy Collins, Arlo Guthrie and others show how the music coming out of New York's Greenwich Village challenged the status quo and promoted social change during the 1960s and '70s.

images.caption: Greenwich Village: Music That Defined a Generation (2012)
Greenwich Village: Music That Defined a Generation (2012)

titles.title: High Tech, Low Life
titles.plot: Two Chinese bloggers are a contrast in styles; one uses the medium for self-promotion, the other seeks justice for the poor.

titles.title: How to Die in Oregon
titles.plot: This documentary explores real life responses to Oregon's "Death with Dignity Act," the first law in the U.S. to allow physicians to prescribe lethal doses of drugs to the terminally ill. A middle-aged woman with terminal liver cancer, prepares to take her own life, while another cancer patient decides to suffer through his illness even though death is just as certain for him. Others grapple with choosing their own course of action, and one man decides to hold a "death party."

titles.title: How to Eat Your Watermelon in White Company (And Enjoy It)
titles.original_title: How to Eat Your Watermelon in White Company (And Enjoy It)
titles.plot: Melvin Van Peebles was one of the first black directors to challenge the white establishment in his films, which include "Watermelon Man" and "Sweet Sweetback's Baadasssss Song." In this documentary, the life of Van Peebles is discussed, including his work not only in film, but also as a novelist, actor, musician, stock trader and even Air Force pilot. Interview subjects include Gil Scott-Heron, Spike Lee and Melvin's son and fellow filmmaker, Mario Van Peebles.

images.caption: How to Eat Your Watermelon in White Company (And Enjoy It) (2005)

titles.title: Howard Zinn: You Can't Be Neutral on a Moving Train
titles.original_title: Howard Zinn: You Can't Be Neutral on a Moving Train
titles.plot: Born in 1922, Howard Zinn began his career as a political activist at age 18, when he worked as a labor organizer. In this documentary, the late historian tells his life story. After serving in World War II, Zinn becomes a professor at Atlanta's Spelman College, only to be fired for his activist agitation. Admirers and friends of the fiercely liberal Zinn testify to his impact on their lives as he discusses his commitment to anti-war politics and rethinking American history.

images.caption: Howard Zinn: You Can't Be Neutral on a Moving Train (2004)

titles.title: Human Nature
titles.plot: A scientific discovery called CRISPR gives people the power to change what it means to be human.

titles.title: I Am Jane Doe
titles.plot: American mothers wage a battle against sex trafficking on behalf of their daughters.

titles.title: Les aventuriers voyageurs - Amsterdam et les Pays-Bas : au fil de l'eau
titles.original_title: Les aventuriers voyageurs - Amsterdam et les Pays-Bas : au fil de l'eau
titles.plot: Discovering Amsterdam, a vibrant city with more canals than Venice. A city with iconic windmills, flower-filled fields and countless cycle paths and cultural richness. Exploring canal-lined streets, wind down country roads, cruise through picturesque towns and enjoying local cuisine.

titles.title: Love Means Zero
titles.plot: Tennis coach Nick Bollettieri's relentless desire to win at all costs leads to the destruction of an important relationship.

titles.title: Mango House
titles.plot: A fly-on-the-wall documentary following P.J. Parmar, a medical doctor, and founder of Mango House, the largest shared space for refugees in Colorado and the greater west. Mango House includes a medical clinic, dental clinic, shops, food court, event spaces and Scout Troops for boys and girls. Run for, and by, refugees, it's a safe haven for refugees to feel at home and to thrive.

titles.title: Meteors
titles.plot: A meteor shower coincides with the military lockdown of a Turkish city.

titles.title: Modulations
titles.plot: Filmmaker Iara Lee combines interviews, concert clips and archival footage to chronicle electronic music.

titles.title: Music From the Big House
titles.plot: Singer Rita Chiarelli performs for inmates at a Louisiana prison.

titles.title: My Octopus Teacher
titles.plot: A diver swims with an octopus that lives in a kelp forest off the coast of South Africa.

titles.title: Next Goal Wins
titles.plot: Dutch coach Thomas Rongen attempts the nearly impossible task of turning the American Samoa soccer team from perennial losers into winners.

titles.title: Of Medicine and Miracles
titles.plot: Following Dr. Carl June as he attempts to find a cure for cancer; all of June's research and work are on the line when 6-year-old Emily Whitehead becomes the first child to enroll in his experimental trial.

titles.title: On The Wing
titles.plot: The impact of WWII on members of the 15th Air Force through personal interviews and visual content; the training these flyers endured, the danger of every sortie and the cost of war in these hostile skies.

titles.title: Passion
titles.plot: Actor John Turturro examines the musical culture of Naples, Italy, in this documentary. Arguing that the city's music has been influenced by its many residents and invaders, from the ancient Greeks to American troops occupying the country after World War II, Turturro presents musicians performing both old and new material. Among the artists are sultry singer M'barka ben Taleb, and saxophonist James Senese, whose Italian mother and unknown black American father equally inform his work.

titles.title: Personal Best
titles.plot: Filmmaker Sam Blair spends four years filming up-and-coming British sprinters as they train to compete in the 2012 Olympic games.

titles.title: Prosecuting Evil: The Extraordinary World of Ben Ferencz
titles.original_title: Prosecuting Evil: The Extraordinary World of Ben Ferencz
titles.plot: Ben Ferencz, the last surviving Nuremberg Trial prosecutor, continues his lifelong crusade for law and peace.

titles.title: Rabin in His Own Words
titles.plot: The life of Yitzhak Rabin.

titles.title: Religulous
titles.plot: Commentator-comic Bill Maher plays devil's advocate with religion as he talks to believers about their faith. Traveling around the world, Maher examines the tenets of Christianity, Judaism and Islam and raises questions about homosexuality, proof of Christ's existence, Jewish Sabbath laws, violent Muslim extremists.

titles.title: Reset
titles.plot: Renowned choreographer and dancer Benjamin Millepied attempts to rejuvenate the Paris Opera Ballet in his position as director.

titles.title: Romántico
titles.plot: Filmmaker Mark Becker examines the plight of Carmelo Muñiz Sánchez who, along with his friend Arturo, ekes out a living as a mariachi musician in San Francisco. When Carmelo returns to his native Mexico, he finds it much harder to earn enough money to support his family, and he ponders chancing another illegal crossing into California.

titles.title: Semper Fi: Always Faithful
titles.plot: Jerry Ensminger pursues evidence of toxic chemicals in the drinking water at Camp Lejeune and exposes the military cover-up of the disaster.

titles.title: Small Town Gay Bar
titles.plot: The lives of gays in the Deep South are explored in this documentary, which looks at two bars in rural Mississippi that cater to a homosexual clientele. "Rumors" is in all other ways a modest neighborhood hangout; "Crossroads" is an anything-goes establishment. Interviews with regular patrons portray both bars as islands of acceptance in an ocean of prejudice, exemplified by the derision of customers at nearby straight bars and the cutting homophobia of anti-gay preacher Fred Phelps.

titles.title: Stevie Nicks: In Your Dreams
titles.plot: Singer and songwriter Stevie Nicks works on her latest album.

titles.title: Super Duper Alice Cooper
titles.plot: Rare archival footage, animation and interviews illustrate the story of how Vincent Furnier, a preacher's son, became rock icon Alice Cooper.

titles.title: Sweet Dreams
titles.plot: Members of Rwanda's only women's drumming troupe form a partnership with two American entrepreneurs to open Rwanda's first ice cream shop.

titles.title: Talihina Sky: The Story of Kings of Leon
titles.original_title: Talihina Sky: The Story of Kings of Leon
titles.plot: Filmmaker Stephen C. Mitchell goes behind the scenes to document the rise of Tennessee rock band Kings of Leon.

images.caption: Talihina Sky: The Story of Kings of Leon (2011)
Talihina Sky: The Story of Kings of Leon (2011)

titles.title: The Inheritors
titles.plot: Filmmaker Eugenio Polgovsky examines child labor in Mexico.

titles.title: The Love We Make
titles.plot: In October 2001, documentary filmmakers Albert Maysles and Bradley Kaplan follow Paul McCartney around post-9/11 Manhattan as he prepares for the Concert for New York City. The concert, held at Madison Square Garden, was organized by McCartney as a benefit for the survivors of fallen firemen, police and first responders, and featured musical performances, short films, and speeches. David Bowie, Billy Joel, the Who, Mick Jagger, Keith Richards, James Taylor and many others performed.

titles.title: The Road to Fame
titles.plot: Filmmaker Hao Wu follows students in China as they audition for a production of the American musical "Fame."

titles.title: The Secret Disco Revolution
titles.plot: Alice Echols, Michael Musto, Gloria Gaynor, Thelma Houston and others appear in filmmaker Jamie Kastner's exploration of disco music's empowerment of women, blacks and homosexuals.

titles.title: The Weird World of Blowfly
titles.plot: Miami musician Clarence Reid sings raunchy tunes on his world tours.

titles.title: The Work
titles.plot: Set inside a single room in Folsom Prison, three men from the outside participate in a four-day group therapy retreat with level-four convicts. Over the four days, each man in the room takes his turn at delving deep into his past.

titles.title: Unbranded
titles.plot: Four friends travel across public land from Mexico to Canada with 16 horses.

titles.title: Valley of Tears
titles.plot: In 1979, documentarian Hart Perry begins chronicling striking Latino laborers in Raymondville, Texas, who demand an increase in minimum wage from the 25 cents per bag of onions picked they had been receiving for more than 20 years. In the 1990s, he returns during a controversial school board election as the Latino community struggles to elect a candidate of their own to the all-white board. In 2000, Perry comes back again to cover lawyer Juan Guerra's campaign for district attorney.

titles.title: Wasted! The Story of Food Waste
titles.original_title: Wasted! The Story of Food Waste
titles.plot: Every year 1.3 billion tons of food is thrown away. Filmmakers explore the reasons for this waste and ways to fix the problem.

titles.title: Watchers of the Sky
titles.plot: The life of Raphael Lemkin, the man who first used the term genocide.

titles.title: We Jam Econo: The Story of the Minutemen
titles.original_title: We Jam Econo: The Story of the Minutemen
titles.plot: Through interviews and archival footage, director Tim Irwin documents the history of the influential 1980s punk band the Minutemen. Surviving band members Mike Watt and George Hurley provide a firsthand look into the band's world, from their start in San Pedro to the 1985 death of D. Boon, the band's co-founding member. Numerous musicians, including Henry Rollins, Thurston Moore, and Red Hot Chili Peppers bassist Flea, offer insight into the Minutemen's importance to the punk scene.

titles.title: WMD: Weapons of Mass Deception
titles.plot: Filmmaker Danny Schechter examines media coverage of the war in Iraq.
